issues.description: Method name mismatch for the order-processing method: the problem statement (UML and textual requirements) requires a method named checkOrderReady() that orderMeal() should call to attempt serving queued orders. The solution implementation provides a method named processOrders() and orderMeal() calls processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(). This naming inconsistency between the spec and the reference implementation can confuse students about which method to implement and where the order-serving logic should live.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred for aligning with the spec): rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady() and update orderMeal() to call checkOrderReady(). Update any tests or examples to use checkOrderReady(). Option B: if the name processOrders() is preferred, update the problem statement (UML and textual references) to require processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady(). Ensure the template, spec, and reference implementation all use the same method name so students implement the expected API.
